conf.description: IBM Guardium DAM policy-violation-alerts, syslog-cef: strips the Guardium/SQLGUARD syslog wrapper, parses the CEF header+extension by regex (the cef function only serializes, it cannot parse), resolves cs1/cs2 via their csNLabel companions, un-inverts src/dst for exception events, and normalizes severity/action/outcome per recommendations.direct.cribl.

conf.comment: Guardium real-time alert, shipped CEF template. Parser must key on the CEF: banner (site can flip to LEEF) and tolerate APAR GA17140's extra space after CEF:.

functions.description: Peel the Guardium syslog header hostname and the quoted SQLGUARD ALERT subject, and locate the CEF record (tolerant of the GA17140 extra space)
Split the CEF pipe-delimited header into its positional fields and isolate the extension blob

Extract every extension key by fixed position with bounded lazy groups instead of a naive space-delimited kv split: Guardium extension values such as cs2 (MS SQL SERVER), proto (Named Pipes) and sproc (JDBC THIN CLIENT) carry unescaped spaces that a generic kvp parser would truncate

conf.code: var __labels = {}; if (__e['cs1Label']) { __labels[__e['cs1Label']] = __e['cs1']; } if (__e['cs2Label']) { __labels[__e['cs2Label']] = __e['cs2']; } var __sev = __labels['Severity']; if (__sev === 'INFO') { __e['event.severity'] = 1; } else if (__sev === 'LOW') { __e['event.severity'] = 3; } else if (__sev === 'MED') { __e['event.severity'] = 5; } else if (__sev === 'HIGH') { __e['event.severity'] = 8; } var __srvType = __labels['Server Type']; if (__srvType !== undefined) { __e['guardium.alert.server_type'] = __srvType; } var __actRaw = __e['act']; var __actionMap = {'0':'unknown','1':'sql_access','2':'sql_error','3':'login_failed','8':'rpc','9':'sql_success','11':'raw_statement','12':'bind_data','15':'data_value'}; var __action = (__actRaw !== undefined && __actionMap[String(__actRaw)] !== undefined) ? __actionMap[String(__actRaw)] : (typeof __actRaw === 'string' ? __actRaw.toLowerCase() : undefined); if (__action !== undefined) { __e['event.action'] = __action; } if (__action === 'sql_error' || __action === 'login_failed') { __e['event.outcome'] = 'failure'; } else if (__action === 'sql_success') { __e['event.outcome'] = 'success'; } var __isException = (__action === 'sql_error' || __action === 'login_failed'); var __srcRaw = __e['src']; var __dstRaw = __e['dst']; var __sptRaw = __e['spt']; var __dptRaw = __e['dpt']; if (__isException) { __e['source.ip'] = __dstRaw; __e['destination.ip'] = __srcRaw; __e['source.port'] = __dptRaw; __e['destination.port'] = __sptRaw; } else { __e['source.ip'] = __srcRaw; __e['destination.ip'] = __dstRaw; __e['source.port'] = __sptRaw; __e['destination.port'] = __dptRaw; } var __proto = __e['proto']; if (typeof __proto === 'string' && __proto.toUpperCase() === 'TCP') { __e['network.transport'] = 'tcp'; } else if (__proto !== undefined) { __e['guardium.alert.local_transport'] = __proto; }

functions.description: Resolve cs1/cs2 through their csNLabel companions rather than hardcoded slots (Global Profile template is site-editable); convert INFO/LOW/MED/HIGH to numeric event.severity (the CEF header severity is a hard-coded constant and must be ignored); normalize numeric/string act to one event.action vocabulary and derive event.outcome only for sql_error/login_failed/sql_success; un-invert src/dst/spt/dpt for those same exception-class events; route non-TCP local transports off network.transport
Batch-rename every status:mapped/status:unmapped field whose source name is a clean identifier straight to its ECS or custom target
Set _time from rt (receiptTimeMills, ms epoch) since @timestamp cannot be targeted directly; tag event.dataset; drop the intermediate/raw fields consumed above
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
